title: From Conjecture to the Lean Kernel: optimal lattices, quantum energies and population genetics — human proofs, Lean 4, rusty-SUNDIALS and LeanFlow (a textbook for university mathematics, physics and engineering students)
description:
A 181-page English university-level edition of the French textbook De la conjecture au noyau Lean (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23665820). The proofs, numbers, confidence levels and caveats are the same; it adds 19 short "University remarks" (standard facts, Tier L) and 10 harder exercises for undergraduate and graduate readers. It tells the story of a year of formalisation as it happened: conjectures, human proofs, Lean 4 statements checked by the kernel, numerical solutions with rusty-SUNDIALS (CVODE in Rust) and LeanFlow certificates, on public Hugging Face datasets, and refutations.

Contents: five chapters (foundations; the flow of formalisations; a quantum surprise from zero-point energy; population genetics in Lean up to the isothermal theorem; five use cases with data, code and certificates), the five hidden acronym theorems with their images, and appendices A–F: analysis, finite Markov chains and martingales, Lean 4 for beginners, certified numerics, a reproduction guide, and 12 worked Python, Rust and LeanFlow examples with real outputs.

Confidence levels (Elenchus). A: kernel-checked Lean (axioms within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, a leanchecker kernel replay passed, and no kernel-bypassing construct found); modules without a recorded replay are marked "A without replay". L: literature. C: a human argument. X: floating point, which never supports a claim.

Honesty. Produced by AI agents (Claude) under the author's direction and audited by separate AI agents (French edition: ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS for chapters and appendices; English edition: ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS), with corrections applied. No human mathematician has reviewed the book. Several results depend on openai/math theorems, which are AI-generated and not peer reviewed. The Sandier–Serfaty conjecture is NOT proved here; the Navier–Stokes chapter reports an independent rebuild and kernel replay of a third-party corpus and claims no Clay problem is solved. Negative results are reported as such. Figures reused from the French edition carry French labels, and code listings and logs are reproduced as run, so their comments are in French.

Dedicated to Ilene, Alexis and Aurelia.
notes: English university edition (v1) of doi:10.5281/zenodo.23665820. Independent audit: papers/textbook_formalisation_2026_en/AUDIT.md, with REVISION.md. Figures and code are shared with the French edition.
